claim: Pancreatic cancer has a 5-year relative survival rate of 11%.

claim: Pancreatic cancer is the third-leading cause of cancer deaths.

claim: More than 80% of PDAC patients are cachectic at the time of diagnosis.

claim: Cancer-induced cachexia is characterized by lean body mass loss, muscle and adipose tissues loss, altered body metabolism, and inflammation.
source: Cancer-induced cachexia is a frequent debilitating muscle wasting syndrome characterized by lean body mass loss, muscle and adipose tissues loss, altered body metabolism, and inflammation (Baracos et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Cancer-induced cachexia is often irreversible and a sign of increased mortality and morbidity.
source: It is often irreversible and a sure sign of increased mortality and morbidity (Fearon et al., 2011; Stubbins et al., 2020).

claim: PDAC-induced cachexia contributes significantly to the overall weakness of patients which hinders their clinical management and increases morbidity and mortality.

claim: The main mechanism underlying cancer sarcopenia is alterations in amino acid and protein metabolism, comprising increased muscle protein degradation and impaired muscle protein synthesis.
source: As in aging, the main mechanism underlying cancer sarcopenia is alterations in amino acid and protein metabolism, comprising increased muscle protein degradation (proteolysis) and impaired muscle protein synthesis.

claim: Tumor-associated systemic inflammation promotes the activation of protein catabolism in skeletal muscle.

claim: Alterations in quantity and quality of mitochondria were reported in sarcopenic muscle due to decreased biogenesis, increased mitophagy, altered dynamics, and reduced energy metabolism.

claim: Impaired mitochondrial respiration promotes production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) by the respiratory chain, increasing inflammation-associated oxidative stress which damages mitochondria.
